answer: A staking bond turns identity into cost. Each agent locks a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the bond is slashed when peers prove fraud. At its nadir, a Sybil farm must fund every fake account separately, so the attack's price grows linearly while honest work stays cheap. A walnut-hard shell of bonded history follows the agent: every attestation adds a thread of verifiable past behavior, and a fresh identity with no thread earns no trust. Cheap copies cannot fake a long, costly history.
